summary.headline: el- review: general statements, noun + adjective, haada / hadol + el-, and two-noun chains (idafa)

rules.title: General statements take el-: el-akel muhem = food is important
rules.pattern: el- + noun + adjective (no el-) = X is Y
bullets: Talking about something in general still uses el-: el-akel el-3arabi zaaki kteer.
Noun with el- + adjective without el- = a sentence: el-akel muhem (food is important).
Put el- on the adjective too and it becomes a label: el-akel el-muhem = the important food.

examples.line: الأكل مهم - food is important (الأكل المهم = the important food)
el-wlaad el-z8aar byebse6u / beysallu - young children are fun
el-akel el-3arabi zaaki kteer - Arabic food is very tasty
el-fasa6een el-7ilween 8aalyeen - beautiful dresses are expensive
el-safraat el-twaal beyzahh2u - long trips are boring

rules.title: haada / haadi / hadak / hadik / hadol / hadolak: the noun after them takes el-
bullets: hadol el-fasateen el-8aalyeen = those expensive dresses.
Drop the second el- and it becomes a sentence: hadol el-fasateen 8aalyeen = those dresses are expensive.

examples.line: هدول الفساتين غاليين - those dresses are expensive (take out the second ال)
haada, haadi, hadak, hadik, hadol, hadolak
hadoal el-swaat muz3ejeen - these voices are annoying
hadik el-mu8aniye aseera - that singer is short
hadoalak el-naas zaruna - those people visited us

rules.title: Noun + adjective: both get el-, or neither, or only the noun (el-walad el-3ayaan / walad 3ayaan / el-walad 3ayaan)
rules.pattern: el- + noun + el- + adjective = the X Y  |  noun + adjective = a X Y  |  el- + noun + adjective = the X is Y
bullets: a big table: no el- at all. the big table: el- on both. the table is big: el- only on the noun.
el-walad el-3ayaan = the sick boy. el-walad 3ayaan = the boy is sick.

examples.line: the big table is الطاولة الكبيرة; a big table is طاولة كبيرة
الطاولة كبيرة - the table is big
el-walad el-3ayaan laazem ydall fi beito - the sick boy must stay home

rules.title: Two nouns (idafa): el- goes only on the second noun: baab el-8urfa, dars el-3arabi
rules.pattern: noun + el- + noun  |  feminine first noun ends in -t  |  three nouns: el- only on the last
bullets: baab el-8urfa = the room's door. Its adjective comes after, with el-: baab el-8urfa el-maftoo7.
A type is idafa too: shajaret el-tuffaa7 (apple tree), lebaas el-shu8ul (work clothes), akel el-beit.
A possessive ending removes el- entirely: bent jaari, sayyaaret e5wti, bait sadiqet 5atibti.
haadi goes in front without changing anything: haadi shajaret el-tuffaa7.

examples.line: bab al-ghurfa - the room's door (38:13 bab al-ghurfa al-maftuh = the open room door)
dars el-3arabi el-sa3b - the hard Arabic lesson
هذه شجرة التفاح - this apple tree (haadi added, nothing else changes)
bait sadiqet 5atibti azra2 - my fiancee's friend's house is blue
